== Old PC website (swccgpc.com) facts added, 24 November 2026 ==
Added a paragraph on his Tournament Support Advocate work from old swccgpc.com news, plus a June 2003 Service row. Sources used: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423222342/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/october02archives.htm October Updates] (24 October 2002); his DecipherCon 2002 wrap-up (already cited as pc-dconwrap); [https://web.archive.org/web/20040620161313/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds Begins in 2003] (late 2002); [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423221707/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/february03archives.htm February Updates] and [https://web.archive.org/web/20030424053234/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/championshipnews02062003.htm 2003 Championship Circuit Opens in One Month] (6 February 2003); [https://web.archive.org/web/20030819162615/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/march03archives.htm March Updates] (23 March 2003); [https://web.archive.org/web/20030810085606/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/april03archives.htm April Updates] (1 April 2003); [https://web.archive.org/web/20030809102648/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/tournamentchanges06182003.htm Upcoming Changes to Decipher's Tournament Software] (June 2003).
=== Missing data ===
* The Road to Worlds 2003 article carries no date; it says "As the New Year approaches", and the 6 February 2003 news calls it "almost two months ago", so the text says "Toward the end of 2002".
* A gap list said he was the contact for PC fundraiser tournament directors in 2003; the 6 February 2003 article does not say that, so it was left out (fundraiser pages from April 2003 could be checked).
=== Build notes ===
* The page keeps a Sources section and a 15-word gallery caption that style_lint flags (HEADING, CAPTION); both were already on the page and were not changed in this edit.

=== Missing data ===
* His forum posts do not say he held a moderator title, so the page does not call him one; he did run the forum clean-up and spoke for the forum staff.
* Not added: his April 2004 post (topic 3123) relaying Decipher's plans for two new proprietary games besides MegaMan. It is about Decipher's products, not his work; it may suit a Decipher or [[WARS TCG]] page.
* Not added: his April 2004 remark about how far he lived from Gen Con. The post does not say it (it only says he would be coming from Chicago), and it is private detail.
* Not added: his December 2002 post in the Asteroids topic (469); it adds nothing beyond the forum handle.

=== Marginal cuts ===
* Not added: David Kangas's critical account of October 2004 (topic 4063, post 55368) about the 2003 World Championship arrangements and Howard's retirement. It is one player's hostile opinion; under the forum rules it is left out.

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* The insert-card ruling: Damian Loback says Howard told him at Dragon*Con that inserts were legal in Classic; Nick Kolnik says he was there and that the ban list was updated afterwards; Howard confirms on 19 September 2003. The ruling's exact date at Dragon*Con 2003 is not given.
